title: Cooperative exploration and target search
role: Graduate Researcher · Advisor: Dr. Srikanth Saripalli
summary: Multi-robot exploration integrating shared mapping, frontier allocation, navigation and visual target detection.
challenge: A multi-robot exploration system for coordinating a Husky and two Jackals in an initially unknown environment. Shared mapping connects frontier selection, task allocation and autonomous navigation, while visual detection supports target search.
contributions: Mapping and localization

Integrated Extended Kalman Filter localization using odometry and inertial measurements, with LiDAR observations contributing to a shared occupancy map. This provides the motion estimates and spatial information needed for coordinated exploration.
Task allocation

Implemented Wavefront Frontier Detection to identify unexplored boundaries and balanced Hungarian assignment to distribute destinations. Allocation uses Euclidean travel-cost estimates and per-robot capacities, with reassignment when navigation goals cannot be completed.
Navigation and visual search

Connected cost-aware A* global planning with Model Predictive Path Integral local control. Integrated pretrained YOLO inference through PyTorch/CUDA, confirming detections across successive frames before reporting a target.
outcome: Integrated localization, mapping, allocation, navigation and target detection. Ongoing research addresses capability-aware allocation and semantic viewpoint selection.
imageAlt: Exploration workflow: EKF localization supports shared LiDAR mapping, wavefront frontier detection, Hungarian task allocation, and A* planning and MPPI control. Camera-based target detection runs alongside exploration.
imageCaption: Shared mapping and task allocation coordinate exploration while visual detection identifies the target.

title: Automated Perception and Planning for Rural Roads
eyebrow: Autonomous Vehicles for All · Perception & planning
role: Graduate Research Assistant · Advisor: Dr. Reza Langari
status: Vehicle-oriented ROS 2 implementation · recorded-data and simulation workflows
summary: ROS 2 perception and trajectory planning for marked and unmarked rural roads, with a complementary map-based driver-assistance prototype.
imageAlt: Annotated AVA research vehicle with its sensor locations
imageCaption: AVA research vehicle and sensor layout. Project scope: perception and motion planning.
challenge: Rural-road driving requires useful road boundaries even when lane markings are weak or absent. This work combines camera and LiDAR perception with road-relative trajectory planning, alongside a separate OpenStreetMap prototype that provides route context and driver alerts from recorded vehicle positions.
contributions: Road and lane perception

Integrated CLRerNet lane detection, SAM2 image segmentation and SphereFormer LiDAR semantic segmentation. Projected LiDAR measurements into the camera frame to recover spatial road boundaries; extracted left/right road edges from segmented point clouds for downstream processing.
Multisensor object processing

Integrated YOLOv9 detections with synchronized LiDAR and radar observations to associate image objects with spatial detections. ROS 2 messages carry object and boundary outputs, with visualization supporting inspection of the perception pipeline.
Local trajectory planning

Developed Frenet-frame candidate generation with lateral quintic and longitudinal quartic polynomials. Weighted costs balance smoothness, duration, lateral offset and target-speed error; a reference-generation node provides pose, speed and curvature targets to downstream control. Separate configurations support GPS-reference and perception-assisted planning.
Map-based driver assistance

Built an OpenStreetMap route-analysis and driver-information workflow using recorded odometry. Route-segment matching drives intersection and curve warnings, lane and speed-limit displays, and rule-based speed advisories, with explicit labels for inferred map attributes. This prototype is separate from the trajectory-planner control loop.
Visual-representation analysis
Applied Principal Component Analysis to OpenDriveVLA features from 6,019 nuScenes samples. The study measures feature redundancy to inform further investigation of compact visual representations.
outcome: The implementation provides ROS 2 modules for road perception, multisensor object processing and local trajectory references, plus a separate recorded-odometry driver-assistance dashboard. In the feature-analysis study, approximately ten principal components retained 80% of scene-token variance and 97% of map-token variance.

title: Precision Vehicle Tracking and Disturbance Recovery
date: 2024 concept study · 2026 tracking and recovery study
summary: Constrained vehicle tracking using reference-scheduled model predictive control.
challenge: A model predictive control study for vehicle trajectory tracking under steering, acceleration and speed constraints. A reference-scheduled prediction model is evaluated against a nonlinear vehicle simulation, including startup errors and external disturbances.
contributions: Prediction model
Formulated along-track, cross-track, heading and speed errors relative to a time-indexed reference. Scheduled the local prediction model using reference speed and curvature over a 20-step horizon.
Constrained control

Implemented a sparse quadratic program using OSQP with steering, acceleration, command-rate and speed bounds. The controller applies the first optimized input and replans every 100 ms of simulated time.
Validation

Evaluated variable-speed oval, figure-eight and disturbed lane-change scenarios using a nonlinear kinematic bicycle model. Measured tracking and recovery performance alongside independent checks of command and sampled-speed limits.
outcome: All 1,520 optimization solves succeeded across three kinematic simulation scenarios. Position RMSE ranged from 0.289 to 0.396 m, including startup recovery; configured constraint checks passed.
resources: Precision Vehicle Tracking and Disturbance Recovery · theoretical report
sourceNote: Builds on concepts from Mark Misin’s study.

title: Robotic welding automation
role: Graduate Research Assistant · Advisor: Dr. Prabhakar Pagilla
summary: CAD-guided robotic welding with part registration, torch-pose planning and coordinated execution.
challenge: A CAD-guided robotic welding platform that connects workpiece geometry to torch motion and welder commands. The documented implementation covers registration, planning and execution before the later closed-loop process-control extension.
contributions: Registration and geometry

Developed a workflow for pairing CAD features with measured workpiece points and registering them to the robot frame. Selected seam geometry supplies welding targets, torch-orientation hints and approach/retreat waypoints.
Motion generation

Integrated pose interpolation, MoveIt planning and trajectory timing based on the requested travel speed. Joint-motion diagnostics and reconstructed tool positions support inspection of the planned motion.
Operator interface and execution

Combined PyQt5 and RViz with robot execution and welder voltage, wire-feed and trigger commands. The interface brings geometry selection, motion visualization and coordinated hardware operation into one workflow.
outcome: Integrated CAD-to-robot execution with trajectory diagnostics and tool-position logging. Later work added infrared monitoring and process feedback for travel-speed and arc-voltage regulation.
sourceNote: Technical explanation based on the project report and the pre-closed-loop implementation supplied for review. Report figures document this earlier platform. The later process-feedback extension is described separately; proprietary source code is not distributed.

title: Robot motion and feedback control at MIKO
summary: Modeling, feedback control and hardware integration for interactive robots at MIKO.
challenge: Robotics engineering work spanning expressive head articulation, self-balancing mobility and audio-directed orientation. Development connected mechanism modeling and feedback control with sensor integration and physical prototype testing.
contributions: Articulation control
Used measured mechanism responses to inform dynamic models and robust controller design for a head-motion manipulator. Developed motion-planning and control software for expressive joint movement.
Self-balancing hardware

Integrated the sensor suite of a self-balancing robot and tuned feedback controllers for balance regulation. Evaluated stability and motion on the physical platform to connect model-based design with hardware behavior.
Interactive orientation
Mapped audio direction-of-arrival estimates to yaw-axis targets so the robot could orient toward an active speaker. Added remote-control functionality for the mobile platform.
outcome: Developed and evaluated motion-control functionality through system modeling, sensor integration and hardware testing. The linked demonstration shows a prototype from this work.
sourceNote: The demonstration shows a self-balancing prototype, not a specific commercial MIKO product.

title: Robust control for vehicle platooning
summary: Robust longitudinal and lateral control for a simulated three-vehicle platoon.
imageAlt: Master's thesis plot of lateral tracking error using super-twisting control
imageCaption: Lateral tracking error with super-twisting control, reproduced from the master's thesis.
challenge: A master’s thesis comparing longitudinal spacing and lateral tracking controllers for a leader–two-follower vehicle platoon. The simulation study examines how nonlinear control choices affect tracking accuracy, convergence and control effort.
contributions: Dynamics and estimation
Modeled the three-vehicle system in MATLAB/Simulink using nonlinear bicycle dynamics at a reference speed of 8 m/s. Implemented a Luenberger observer to estimate yaw rate from lateral velocity.
Controller development

Compared PID, conventional sliding-mode control, the thesis’s power-rate reaching-law formulation (PREL), and second-order super-twisting control. Evaluated both longitudinal spacing and lateral path-following behavior.
Performance comparison

Compared integral absolute and squared tracking errors, their time-weighted forms, and control-effort measures. This distinguishes accurate tracking from solutions that require greater actuation effort.
outcome: PREL achieved the lowest error indices in the documented simulation. Super-twisting provided lateral convergence without overshoot and the lowest longitudinal control-energy metric. Related publication: ACODS 2022.

title: A robot swarm searching for light
summary: Particle-swarm light-source search implemented on three LEGO NXT robots.
imageAlt: LEGO NXT robot carrying an ArUco tracking marker
imageCaption: LEGO NXT platform with an ArUco marker for overhead tracking.
challenge: A physical light-source search experiment using three LEGO NXT robots and Particle Swarm Optimization. Shared light observations guide collective search, supported by camera-based localization and centralized motion commands.
contributions: Search algorithm
Developed the particle-swarm search in MATLAB and implemented the hardware workflow in Python. Each robot combines its best light observation with the best observation shared by the team.
Localization and communication
Tracked robot positions using an overhead camera and ArUco markers. A centralized controller sends motion targets over Bluetooth, connecting optimization updates to physical robot movement.
Navigation and sensing

Integrated light sensing, waypoint following and ultrasonic obstacle avoidance. Hardware trials evaluated whether the robots could converge toward the brightest region while operating within the experimental arena.
outcome: The robots converged toward the brightest region; one documented trial took 11 iterations. The related paper received a Best Paper Award at ICECA 2019.

title: EKF-SLAM and embedded robot navigation
eyebrow: IIT Bombay internship · Estimation & embedded control
role: Summer intern · Joint project with Alden J. Joseph
summary: Joint robot-pose and landmark estimation in MATLAB, with a separate embedded navigation exercise.
imageAlt: MATLAB EKF-SLAM simulation showing a robot path and landmark estimates
imageCaption: EKF-SLAM simulation from the internship report, showing a waypoint route and estimated landmarks.
challenge: An internship project investigating joint robot-pose and landmark estimation through EKF-SLAM simulation. A separate embedded implementation explores obstacle avoidance and encoder-based motion feedback on a SPARK-V robot.
contributions: Probabilistic estimation
Adapted a MATLAB EKF-SLAM simulator to estimate robot pose and landmark positions together. Implemented prediction and measurement updates with Jacobian-based uncertainty propagation.
Landmark association

Applied uncertainty-aware nearest-neighbor matching with Mahalanobis gating to associate range–bearing measurements with landmarks. Examined how revisiting landmarks changes uncertainty in the estimated map.
Embedded navigation

Extended simulated reactive steering and separately programmed ultrasonic obstacle avoidance and encoder feedback in Embedded C. The SPARK-V implementation used its ATmega16 controller for room-traversal experiments.
outcome: Repeated landmark observations reduced map uncertainty in simulation. The SPARK-V robot separately demonstrated room traversal with obstacle avoidance.

title: Needle-tip tracking with Kalman filtering
summary: Ultrasound needle tracking using robust image processing and Kalman filtering.
challenge: An ultrasound needle-tracking pipeline combining robust image processing with temporal state estimation. Developed in LabVIEW, the system estimates needle-tip position under noisy image conditions and compares performance against an independent electromagnetic reference.
contributions: Needle-feature extraction

Built background-subtraction and edge-detection stages to isolate candidate needle features within a region of interest. Applied Random Sample Consensus line fitting to reduce the influence of speckle and unrelated image edges.
Temporal estimation
Integrated a four-state Kalman filter to combine predicted state with image measurements across frames. This reduces reliance on individual noisy observations when estimating needle-tip position.
Experimental validation
Evaluated tracking in artificial and biological tissue at insertion depths up to 6.5 cm. Used an NDI-Aurora electromagnetic reference to compare the combined estimator against vision-only tracking.
outcome: Position RMSE fell from 0.79 to 0.03 cm in artificial tissue and from 0.84 to 0.21 cm in biological tissue versus vision-only tracking, under the reported experimental conditions.
